Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

Apple closed at $342.56 on 20 November 2026, about $5.0 trillion of market value, after a fiscal fourth quarter on 2 November that delivered revenue of $114.5bn (+12%), diluted EPS of $2.10 (+14%) and a 47.9% gross margin, with a December-quarter guide of 45-46% gross margin [S151, S152, S150, S149, S153]. The market has corrected: the S&P 500 at 6,910.39 is 11.9% below its high, the Nasdaq is 18.4% below its high, the VIX is 30.97 at the 99th percentile and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.91% [S8, S18, S9, S10].

The business is not the problem: fiscal 2026 revenue was $478.8bn, up 15%, EPS $8.98, up 20%, and Q4 services set a record $31.6bn [S148, S149, S153]. Apple converts profit into cash at 0.97 times net income, holds $62,173M of net cash and earns 40.3% of gross profit from services [S6, S17]. What has changed is the margin path: the December quarter is guided to 45-46%, below the 47-48% base case [S153].

The price is still the problem. At $342.56 the shares trade at 38.1 times fiscal 2026 EPS and 35.0 times the $9.79 fiscal 2027 estimate; the DCF at 9.0% is $212, the bull case $277, the sum of the parts $177-238 and the base scenario $284, 17% below the close [S152, S7, S97, S146]. A 46% gross margin takes fair value to $270 at 29 times, which would make the first entry tranche the base case rather than a discount to it [S153, S17, S99].

The view is non-consensus on price, not on franchise: the sell side's average target of $345.63 across 39 analysts sits at the spot price [S152]. The last hard test is December-quarter delivery against the guide and the fiscal 2026 10-K.

parameters.markdown:
Apple closed at $342.56 on 20 November 2026, after fiscal fourth-quarter results on 2 November showed revenue of $114.5bn (+12%), diluted EPS of $2.10 (+14%) and a 47.9% gross margin, with the December quarter guided to 45-46% gross margin on 7-10% revenue growth. The market has corrected: the S&P 500 at 6,910.39 is 11.9% below its high, the VIX is 30.97 at the 99th percentile and the ten-year Treasury yields 4.91%, while technology is down 21.0% in a month against 10.8% for the SPY [S151, S152, S150, S149, S153, S8, S9, S10, S12, S25].

The business is not the problem: fiscal 2026 revenue was $478.8bn, up 15%, EPS $8.98, up 20%, Q4 services set a record $31.6bn, cash conversion is 0.97 times net income and net cash is $62,173M. What has changed is the margin path: the December quarter is guided to 45-46%, below the 47-48% base case. The price is still the problem: at $342.56 the shares trade at 38.1 times fiscal 2026 EPS and 35.0 times the $9.79 fiscal 2027 estimate, while the DCF at 9.0% is $212 and the base scenario $284, 17% below the close; a 46% gross margin takes fair value to $270, making the first entry tranche the base case rather than a discount to it [S148, S149, S153, S6, S17, S152, S7, S97, S146, S99].

The sell side's average target sits at the spot price, so the view is non-consensus on price, not franchise. The core positives are the services annuity, 0.97x cash conversion and the net-cash balance sheet; the key risks are faster margin normalisation, the search-payment appeal and a multiple de-rating. Positioning is zero today, with a first tranche at $270, a second at $245 and a 5% cap below $225; the next hard test is December-quarter delivery and the fiscal 2026 10-K, and follow-up diligence is the working-capital and intangibles note, a primary consensus feed for fiscal 2027 EPS, and the D.C. Circuit briefing [S6, S7, S152].

This report is for research only and is not investment advice.
